title: Driver position fanout to rider sockets
name: Trip position fanout

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this fanout manages rider connections and their subscriptions? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A rider's phone is on a poor network and its socket has 400 KB queued. A new driver position arrives for its trip. What happens?
choices: The frame is skipped for that rider and the dropped counter increments
The frame is queued anyway and delivered later
publish throws and other riders on the trip miss the update

questions.prompt: Why is skipping position frames for a slow socket an acceptable policy for this particular stream?
choices: Because ws guarantees eventual delivery of skipped frames
Because each position supersedes the previous one, so a rider only needs the latest
Because riders resend missed positions on reconnect
Because the trip service retries publish on failure

questions.prompt: The serialized frame in publish is built once per call rather than once per subscriber. What is the main effect of that under heavy fanout?
choices: It guarantees all riders get identical ordering across trips
It makes publish safe to call concurrently from multiple threads
It avoids repeated JSON serialization, keeping the per-subscriber cost to a send call
It prevents slow sockets from blocking fast ones
